extracted.intended_audience: academics and public relations educators/practitioners involved in teaching and assessing news release writing
extracted.subtask_description: Developing, validating, and using a rubric to teach and assess students' public relations news release writing, including procedures for consensus building (Delphi), continuous improvement (PDCA), and measurement-system analysis (six sigma/R&R).

rubrics_metrics.name: PDCA Cycle (Plan-Do-Check-Act) for CQI
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Deming's PDCA Cycle (Plan; Do; Check; Act) as a systematic continuous quality improvement procedure to incrementally refine pedagogy, the rubric, and assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan = Define purpose, goals and objectives; Collect data. Do = Identify needs; Propose change; Implement. Check = Monitor, evaluate and analyze change; Compare old and new data. Act = Adjust strategies for improvement; Refine and reinstitute. Emphasize continuous conversations with stakeholders (faculty, professionals) and repeat loops (the paper describes 8 loops applying PDCA to rubric development).

rubrics_metrics.name: Delphi method for reaching consensus
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Delphi method to gather expert input and facilitate consensus among faculty and/or professionals when defining SKAs, pedagogy, rubric categories, and weights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct sequential anonymous rounds: pose questions, collect feedback, summarize without attribution, allow participants to revise responses; continue rounds until convergence. Used both face-to-face (professionals) and by email (faculty) in the study; allowed resolving disagreements about categories, descriptors, and weights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Six sigma two-trial process for rubric measurement capability
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply a two-trial six sigma process (trial 1 and trial 2) to evaluate repeatability (intra-rater) and reproducibility (inter-rater) of rubric scoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: redact student identifiers; randomly select 7–12 papers from multiple sections; have 2–3 instructors grade each paper in Trial 1; record grades; after adequate time for graders to forget scores, repeat grading same papers (Trial 2) by same instructors; compute ranges, averages, EV (repeatability), AV (reproducibility), R&R and %R&R; use UCLR computed from average range * D4 to flag papers needing regrade. Use simple arithmetic-based calculations if desired; follow quality-control constants (D4, K1, K2) from standard texts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement-system acceptance thresholds (%R&R / EV / AV)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpretation thresholds for measurement-system quality: industry guidance applied to rubrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EV measures repeatability (intra-rater) as % of tolerance; AV measures reproducibility (inter-rater) as % of tolerance. %R&R (total intra+inter) should ideally be <10% of tolerance to be acceptable; 10–30% is marginally acceptable; >30% indicates the measurement system needs improvement. Authors note goal of EV (intra-rater) <10% of tolerance for extremely close repeatability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define tolerance and use UCLR to detect out-of-control papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Define tolerance as the difference between highest and lowest possible scores (e.g., 100-point scale tolerance = 100). Compute UCLR (upper control limit for ranges) = average range (R) * D4; if any individual paper's range exceeds UCLR, that paper must be regraded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calculate average of individual ranges across papers and use statistical constant D4 to set UCLR. Regrade papers exceeding UCLR and substitute new values before final analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Random selection and redaction to reduce bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Randomly select student artifacts and redact student names/identifiers before grading to minimize bias and halo effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use an independent student aide to randomize and redact. Do not control for demographics (gender, ethnicity, race) unless germane. Apply across multiple sections where same rubric is used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simple binomial (yes/no) rubric
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial simple rubric with five broadly defined categories using an acceptable/not acceptable (Y/N) scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix A example items: 1) Are key ideas organized effectively? Y/N; 2) Is headline/lead clear and compelling? Y/N; 3) Is news angle compelling? Y/N; 4) Does release use convincing journalistic style? Y/N; 5) Are basics (grammar/mechanics) in place? Y/N. Paper used this as a first iteration and refined it later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: Headline/lead combination (25 points)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether the message in headline/lead is clear and compelling and whether headline properly summarizes and grabs attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subitems: Is the message clear and compelling? Is the headline a complete sentence? Does tense in headline match release topic? Does headline summarize main point? Is organization's name/product mentioned in headline/subhead? Does the headline 'grab' attention? Does the headline summarize information found in lead paragraph? Scoring (Appendix C): 25 = excellent at most items; 21 = good; 19 = adequate; 16 = poor; 13 = none.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: Lead (20 points)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the lead paragraph for clarity, news angle, timeliness, local interest, introduction of news angle, and inclusion of the 5 W's.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subitems: Is the message clear? Is the news angle compelling? Is information timely? Does the first sentence establish local interest? Does it introduce the news angle? Does the lead include who/what/when/where/why? Scoring (Appendix C): 20/17/15/13/10 bands corresponding to excellent/good/adequate/poor/none.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: Organization / key ideas (15 points)
rubrics_metrics.description: Judge whether key ideas are organized effectively and whether paragraphs/quotes support the main message and move the story forward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subitems: Do points support main message? Does the quote in 2nd/3rd paragraph move story forward? Is attribution correct? Do paragraphs have one dominant idea? Overall, is the release well written? Scoring bands: 15/13/11/10/7 for excellent → none.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: Journalistic style and format (25 points)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure conformity to journalistic and professional expectations for style, objectivity, news structure, format, dateline, contact info, slug lines, and boilerplate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subitems: Conformance to Associated Press Style; objectivity; inverted pyramid structure; least important info last; standard format; dateline includes date and location; contact info includes name/title and day/night phone; second/third pages include slug line; pages end in (more) or ###; boilerplate appropriate and includes source for more information. Scoring bands: 25/21/19/16/13.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: Basics — grammar, sentence and paragraph mechanics (15 points)
rubrics_metrics.description: Check spelling, grammar, punctuation, completeness and style of sentences, and factual accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subitems: Words correctly spelled; grammar correct; punctuation correct; sentences complete; sentences short and declarative; release factually accurate. Scoring bands: 15/13/11/10/7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighted scoring and numerical scales (rubric weights)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use weighted point allocations across rubric categories and defined point bands per item to compute total /100.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix B/C weights: Headline/lead 25; Lead 20; Organization 15; Journalistic style/format 25; Basics grammar 15. Each category uses a 5-band descriptive numeric scale (a–e) mapping to specific point values. Total points summed for grade; rubric refinement can adjust numerical scales and weights via Delphi.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric construct validity and ability to differentiate submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: A valid rubric should identify dimensions as targeted skills, differentiate between weak and strong student submissions, and align with pedagogy and professional expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish baseline via professional evaluation (benchmark) and conduct longitudinal tests against that baseline. Use two-way ANOVA to determine if rubric differentiates between known weak/strong papers and assess differences between faculty and professional graders. If rubric cannot tie results to pedagogy or differentiate submissions, refine categories/weights/descriptors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical tests for validation: ANOVA and F test
rubrics_metrics.description: Use statistical analysis to compare grades and variances across grader groups and to assess precision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-way ANOVA can test: significant differences between papers (X vs Y), differences between faculty and professional grading averages, and interactions. Use F test for equal variances on faculty-only grades to detect significant differences in variance between papers. Report precision (e.g., ±14.54 points at 68% confidence) and R-sq metrics as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter-rater reliability improvement via iterative discussion (faculty Delphi rounds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use repeated rating rounds combined with discussion and justification (Delphi-like) among faculty to reduce inter-rater variance and converge on consensus scoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: nine faculty grade same artifact (Round 1 avg and S.D.); discuss high/low scores and defend; regrade (Round 2) leading to reduced SD; continue until consensus (Round 3). Use F test to compare variances between rounds to document improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowing rewrites to support learning and improve measurement precision
rubrics_metrics.description: Permit students to rewrite weak news releases for re-evaluation to promote learning and reduce measurement variance as releases improve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rewriting may improve student learning and decrease variability in rubric scores, leading to more valid and precise assessment of student work.
